## Evolution of Recommenders

**Phase 1: Collaborative Filtering (1990s)**

- Idea: Users who agreed in the past will agree in the future
- *Papers*: Resnick et al. (1994), Sarwar et al. (2001)

**Phase 2: Matrix Factorization (2000s)**

- Idea: Latent factors explain preferences
- *Papers*: Koren et al. (2009) - Netflix Prize winner

**Phase 3: Neural Two-Tower Retrieval (2010s)**

- Idea: Learn user & item embeddings separately
- *Papers*: @covington2016deep - YouTube recommendations, @yi2019sampling - Sampling bias correction

---

## From Ranking to Slates

**Traditional**: Rank individual items

$$
\text{score}(u, i) = f(\text{user}, \text{item})
$$

**Slate Recommendation**: Optimize sets of items jointly

- Diversity constraints
- MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) - Carbonell & Goldstein
- SlateQ - Ie et al. (reinforcement learning for slates)

::: {.fragment}
**Why?** Top-10 lists should be diverse, complementary, and coherent!
:::

---

## GenAI for Recommendation: A Taxonomy

| **Use Case**              | **How GenAI Helps**                 | **Example**                          |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Embeddings                | Better semantic representations     | Sentence transformers for items      |
| Metadata Generation       | Enrich sparse catalogs              | Generate tags, descriptions          |
| Zero-Shot Recommendation  | Cold-start without training data    | LLM suggests items from text         |
| Sequence Modeling         | Next-item prediction                | Transformer-based sequential models  |
| **Page Generation**       | **Create entire recommendation UIs**| **Autoregressive layout design**     |

::: {.fragment}
Today we'll touch all five, focusing on the last.
:::

---

## Why Generation Matters

**Classical RecSys:**
- Pre-defined templates
- Fixed number of rows
- Static layout

**Generative RecSys:**
- Adaptive layouts per user
- Dynamic number of items/rows
- Personalized page structure

::: {.fragment}
*The entire homepage becomes a recommendation!*
:::

## Key Papers: Classical Era

**Collaborative Filtering**
- Resnick et al., "GroupLens: An Open Architecture for Collaborative Filtering" (1994)
- Sarwar et al., "Item-Based Collaborative Filtering" (2001)

**Matrix Factorization**
- Koren et al., "Matrix Factorization Techniques for Recommender Systems" (2009)

**Neural Retrieval**
- Covington et al., "Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations" (2016)

**Ranking & Slates**
- Carbonell & Goldstein, "Maximal Marginal Relevance" (1998)
- Ie et al., "SlateQ" (2019)
